correctness.rationale: Cut switching acts by independently distinguishing sign characters of distinct edges and forces the unique global John ellipsoid to have half-vector center and diagonal positive definite shape. The exact published Barahona--Mahjoub K5-minor-free facet list converts containment to coordinate caps and odd cycle supports. Every induced cycle of length k>=4 is automatically satisfied by the caps because k<=(k-2)^2; triangle sums alone remain. Strictly concave log determinant gives a unique positive optimum, and exact equality of support/slack yields the complete contact classification. Wheel and book formulas satisfy rational KKT certificates. Embedded verify.py checked 22 exact-rational graph instances with 1,522 signed-cycle inequalities on 12,840 cut assignments. Finite instances corroborate but are not a proof for all graphs.

originality.rationale: The direct 1986 K5-minor-free facet theorem, the 2019 minor-free combinatorial classification, and the 2024 cut-polytope 1-skeleton study do not explicitly classify maximal-volume inscribed ellipsoids or their contact hyperplanes. A 2023 source analyzes a different metric polytope and asks about the cut polytope. The new structural implication is that triangle incidence alone determines the diagonal shape, with no longer-cycle restriction for the optimum and an exact facet-contact dichotomy. General methods for inscribed ellipsoids do not alone establish that graph-theoretic simplification. Material primary-source checks and published-result searches revealed no dominating result, but bibliographic equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: A semantically equivalent determinant-optimal design or signed cut-cone ellipsoid classification could appear under different terminology; no complete exhaustive global survey or independent priority verification was possible.
The proof invokes the published K5-minor-free facet description as a premise rather than reproving its full graph-minor theorem.
The mathematical claim does not extend to graphs with a K5 minor or the circumscribed ellipsoid, and numerical tests do not establish universality.

value.rationale: Determines a canonical Euclidean extremal ellipsoid for every finite K5-minor-free graph cut polytope, reducing potentially long and numerous cycle facets to edge-triangle incidence constraints. The result specifies every principal semiaxis, exact volume and all facet contacts, including the distinct quadrilateral equality case and strict exclusion of longer cycles. Nonuniform wheel and triangle-book formulas show concrete shape transitions that are not vertex count/tabulation exercises. The result is a finite strictly concave variational determination for arbitrary graph input rather than a claim of universal radicals or downstream optimization breakthroughs.
